records.jp: そういえば、断片的に思い出したことがあるんです
records.en_original: I'm beginning to remember bits and pieces of things.
records.en_auxiliary: I'm beginning to remember bits and pieces of things.
records.en: Come to think of it, I've started remembering bits and pieces.

records.jp: どんなことですか？
records.en_original: What kind of things?
records.en_auxiliary: What kind of things?
records.en: What did you remember?

records.jp: ある日、学校から帰る時<CR>ビルの前に人だかりができているのを見たんです
records.en_original: One day, on my way home from school, I saw a crowd of people gathered in front of a building.
records.en_auxiliary: One day, on my way home from school, I saw a crowd of people gathered in front of a building.
records.en: One day, on my way home from school,<CR>I saw a crowd gathered in front of a building.

records.jp: どうやらビルの大型ディスプレイでスポーツ中継が<CR>放送されていたみたいで
records.en_original: Apparently, the television on display was showing some kind of sporting event.
records.en_auxiliary: Apparently, the television on display was showing some kind of sporting event.
records.en: It seemed that a sports broadcast<CR>was playing on the building's giant screen.

records.jp: 観客の皆さんは歓声を上げたり野次を飛ばしたり。<CR>選手の一挙一動に反応していました
records.en_original: They were shouting and cheering. They hung on the athlete's every move.
records.en_auxiliary: They were shouting and cheering. They hung on the athlete's every move.
records.en: The spectators cheered and shouted jeers.<CR>They reacted to every single move the athletes made.

records.jp: なぜでしょうか？
records.en_original: Why would that be?
records.en_auxiliary: Why would that be?
records.en: Why?

records.jp: え……なぜって聞かれても
records.en_original: Uhh, I couldn't say...
records.en_auxiliary: Uhh, I couldn't say...
records.en: Huh...? Even if you ask why...

records.jp: だって観客の方々は選手じゃないんですよ。<CR>選手の身内でもないだろうし
records.en_original: The people watching weren't athletes themselves, or even related to the ones shown.
records.en_auxiliary: The people watching weren't athletes themselves, or even related to the ones shown.
records.en: The spectators aren't athletes themselves,<CR>and they're probably not related to them either.

records.jp: スポンサーでもない限り、<CR>試合結果に利益が直接絡むわけでもないですよね
records.en_original: Unless you're a sponsor, you have nothing to gain from the outcome of the game.
records.en_auxiliary: Unless you're a sponsor, you have nothing to gain from the outcome of the game.
records.en: Unless they're sponsors,<CR>the result of the match doesn't directly affect their interests either.

records.jp: 全くの他人の勝敗に<CR>なんであそこまで熱くなれるんですか？
records.en_original: How can people be so passionate about the victory or defeat of a total stranger?
records.en_auxiliary: How can people be so passionate about the victory or defeat of a total stranger?
records.en: Why can they become so passionate<CR>about whether a complete stranger wins or loses?

records.jp: 選手を他人と思ってないからでしょうか
records.en_original: Maybe they don't see the athlete as a stranger.
records.en_auxiliary: Maybe they don't see the athlete as a stranger.
records.en: Maybe it's because they don't see the athlete as a stranger?

records.jp: いや本当は他人なんですけど、取材とかSNSとか、<CR>その人の一部に触れることはあるでしょう？
records.en_original: Well, they may technically be strangers, but I think people feel a kind of connection after watching them through interviews and social media.
records.en_auxiliary: Well, they may technically be strangers, but I think people feel a kind of connection after watching them through interviews and social media.
records.en: They really are strangers, of course, but through interviews, social media,<CR>and such, people can come into contact with parts of who they are, right?

records.jp: そういう機会が増えてくると<CR>親近感が湧いてくるのかなって
records.en_original: When famous people get a lot of exposure like that, other people start to feel a sense of familiarity.
records.en_auxiliary: When famous people get a lot of exposure like that, other people start to feel a sense of familiarity.
records.en: Maybe the more chances they have to see someone,<CR>the more familiar that person starts to feel.

records.jp: 親近感、ですか
records.en_original: Familiarity?
records.en_auxiliary: Familiarity?
records.en: A sense of familiarity?

records.jp: それで選手に自分を重ねているパターンも<CR>ありそうですね
records.en_original: I suppose it's possible that they identify with the athletes.
records.en_auxiliary: I suppose it's possible that they identify with the athletes.
records.en: There may also be cases where spectators<CR>project themselves onto an athlete.

records.jp: 叶えられなかった夢を託す、みたいな
records.en_original: Living out a dream vicariously.
records.en_auxiliary: Living out a dream vicariously.
records.en: Like entrusting them with a dream they could not fulfill themselves.

records.jp: うんうん、そういうこともあると思います。<CR>久野さんはどうですか？
records.en_original: I think that's also part of it. What do you think, Kirara?
records.en_auxiliary: I think that's also part of it. What do you think, Kirara?
records.en: Yes, yes, I think that happens too.<CR>What do you think, Kuno-san?

records.jp: スポーツ番組は一部の人間を操る<CR>電波を発しているのだ
records.en_original: Sports programs are just mind control beams used to control the population.
records.en_auxiliary: Sports programs are just mind control beams used to control the population.
records.en: Sports programs emit radio waves<CR>that control certain humans.

records.jp: 大胆な意見ですね……
records.en_original: That's a bold statement...
records.en_auxiliary: That's a bold statement...
records.en: That's a bold opinion...

records.jp: それに呼応したかしなかったかってだけのこと。<CR>彼らの気持ちが分からなくたって気にすることはない
records.en_original: Some people respond to it, and others don't. Don't bother trying to understand how they feel.
records.en_auxiliary: Some people respond to it, and others don't. Don't bother trying to understand how they feel.
records.en: I see.<CR>Maybe that's why my heart races.

records.jp: 星崎さんはどう思いますか？
records.en_original: What do you think, Ao?
records.en_auxiliary: What do you think, Ao?
records.en: What do you think, Hoshizaki-san?

records.jp: 私も詩帆さんの意見に賛成かな
records.en_original: I agree with Shiho.
records.en_auxiliary: I agree with Shiho.
records.en: I think I agree with Shiho-san.

records.jp: スポーツ選手を推しに置き換えたら理解できた
records.en_original: I guess it's kind of like picking a favorite character in a manga.
records.en_auxiliary: I guess it's kind of like picking a favorite character in a manga.
records.en: Once I replaced the athlete with an oshi, I understood.

records.jp: どの分野でもきっとそうですよね
records.en_original: Once you have a favorite, you want to root for them.
records.en_auxiliary: Once you have a favorite, you want to root for them.
records.en: It must be the same in any field.

records.jp: 実生活で会う人たちみたいにお互いを認知して、<CR>分かり合ったりすることはできなくても
records.en_original: Even though you'll never meet them, and they'll never know who you are...
records.en_auxiliary: Even though you'll never meet them, and they'll never know who you are...
records.en: Even if you can't know and understand each other<CR>the way people who meet in real life can,

records.jp: でも、あの人のここには共感できる。応援したい。<CR>そういう関係があってもいいと思います
records.en_original: I can still relate to them, and I want to support them. I think it's okay to have that kind of relationship.
records.en_auxiliary: I can still relate to them, and I want to support them. I think it's okay to have that kind of relationship.
records.en: you can still relate to something about them and want to support them.<CR>I think that kind of relationship is fine too.

records.jp: 私も詩さんの意見に賛成かな
records.en_original: I agree with Uta.
records.en_auxiliary: I agree with Uta.
records.en: I think I agree with Uta-san.

records.jp: 私みたいな平凡な人間は「こんな人に生まれたら」とか<CR>すぐ妄想して気持ち良くなっちゃうよね
records.en_original: I think regular people like me often like to fantasize about what it would be like if they were born as someone else.
records.en_auxiliary: I think regular people like me often like to fantasize about what it would be like if they were born as someone else.
records.en: Ordinary people like me quickly start fantasizing,<CR>"What if I had been born as someone like that?" and enjoying the thought.

records.jp: でも星崎さんは今のままがいいと思います
records.en_original: But I think you're fine just the way you are, Ao.
records.en_auxiliary: But I think you're fine just the way you are, Ao.
records.en: But I think Hoshizaki-san is best just as she is now.

records.jp: 他の人みたいになってしまったら……<CR>なんか、もやもやってします
records.en_original: I don't think I would like it if you became someone else.
records.en_auxiliary: I don't think I would like it if you became someone else.
records.en: If you became like someone else...<CR>it would leave me feeling somehow unsettled.

records.jp: （「さみしい」ってことなのかな？<CR>だったらありがたく受け取ろう）
records.en_original: (Does she mean that she'd miss me? I'll take that as a compliment)
records.en_auxiliary: (Does she mean that she'd miss me? I'll take that as a compliment)
records.en: (Does that mean she would feel lonely?<CR>If so, I will gratefully accept it.)

records.jp: 私もきららの意見に賛成。<CR>熱に浮かされたみたいになってる人いるもんね
records.en_original: I agree with Kirara. People get way too fired up about sports.
records.en_auxiliary: I agree with Kirara. People get way too fired up about sports.
records.en: I agree with Kirara too.<CR>Some people really do act as though they are delirious with fever.

records.jp: うむ。でも楽しいならいいと思う。<CR>きららも楽しそうにしてるのを見るのは好き
records.en_original: Yes. Though I suppose it's all right as long as they're having fun. I enjoy watching people get excited about it.
records.en_auxiliary: Yes. Though I suppose it's all right as long as they're having fun. I enjoy watching people get excited about it.
records.en: Indeed. But Kirara thinks it's fine as long as they're having fun.<CR>Kirara likes seeing people enjoy themselves too.

records.jp: ただし、面白いから見ろと強制されるのは勘弁
records.en_original: I just wish they would stop trying to get me to enjoy it.
records.en_auxiliary: I just wish they would stop trying to get me to enjoy it.
records.en: Kirara doesn't want to be forced to watch just because they call it interesting.

records.jp: そう、それ
records.en_original: Yeah, totally!
records.en_auxiliary: Yeah, totally!
records.en: Yes, exactly that.

records.jp: でもぶっちゃけあんまスポーツ興味ないからなぁ。<CR>本当のところ、よくわかんないんだよね
records.en_original: But to be honest, I'm really not that into sports so I guess I don't know the real answer.
records.en_auxiliary: But to be honest, I'm really not that into sports so I guess I don't know the real answer.
records.en: But honestly, I'm not that interested in sports.<CR>So I don't really know the answer either.

records.jp: 私もそれでわからなくて質問したんです
records.en_original: I feel the same. That is why I asked.
records.en_auxiliary: I feel the same. That is why I asked.
records.en: I didn't understand it either. That's why I asked.

records.jp: わたしもです
records.en_original: Me too.
records.en_auxiliary: Me too.
records.en: Neither did I.

records.jp: 右に同じ
records.en_original: Same.
records.en_auxiliary: Same.
records.en: Same here.

records.jp: ……こういうとこ、うちら気合うね
records.en_original: I guess we all have that in common...
records.en_auxiliary: I guess we all have that in common...
records.en: ...We really click in ways like this.

records.jp: そうかもしれませんね
records.en_original: So it seems.
records.en_auxiliary: So it seems.
records.en: Maybe we do.
